column1: # libsa1 boundary stub policy (sadc docs/libsa1_integration.md 10.5, decision D8).
# One line per function that the lowered game code calls or takes the address of and that no lowered
# translation unit defines: pclower's "stubs" (report.json; build/pclower/report.json after a build).
# LIB/gen/gen_stubs.py turns this file into C (build/gen/sa1g_stubs_policy.c), linked into libsa1 instead
# of pclower's all-fatal sa1g_stubs.c. Functions that are decompiled later are lowered by pclower and
# drop out of its stub list: their lines here are then reported as stale and ignored (never stubbed).
# Columns (tab-separated): addr  name  sig  policy  evidence
#   addr      DC address (as pclower reports it)
#   name      symbol of the stub (the code map entry and the C function)
#   sig       pclower ABI signature "ret:args" (v i8 u8 i16 u16 i32 u32 p f32 f64 gfn); the generator warns
#   policy    fatal            record the DC address, longjmp to the tick: SA1_ERR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED and an
#                              SA1_EVENT_UNIMPLEMENTED event (the default for a stub without a line)
#             ret <value>      return a constant (integer, or a float literal for f32)
#             address-only     the address is stored or handed over but libsa1 never calls it: a no-op
#                              (returns 0) so a stray call is harmless
#             freetask         exec of a task created by game code: FreeTask(tp) (design 10.5: "exec that
#                              push SA1_EVENT_<KIND> (include/libsa1.h) into the ticking world's queue and
#                              return V (default 0 for non-void functions). X = aN (argument N, from 0) or a
#                              constant; P = aN,aM,aK (three float arguments), aN@twp (taskwk * argument:
#                              its pos at +0x20) or aN@vec (NJS_POINT3 * argument); positions are in SA1 space,
#                              (0,0,0) when absent. arg defaults to the DC address of the stub, bank to 0.
#   evidence  why (design section, callers, what the call log of the reference simulator shows):
#             "ref:"   calls of the original during logic steps (S phase) in the 15 reference scripts
#                      (harness/tests/sim: harness trace --log-sdk with this list as --sdk-list), return values
#                      seen; "frame code" = calls outside the steps (libsa1 never runs those)
#             "reach:" static reach from the character mains and the libsa1 step functions (pad 8C050BE4,
#                      over build/1ST_READ.xrefs.json (direct calls and literal-pool code addresses; pointers in
#                      data tables are not followed, so "none" is a strong hint, not a proof)
#             "FIDELITY": a constant policy cannot reproduce the original's side effects (rand draws, tasks);
#                      such stubs are the first decompilation candidates when a reference script reaches them
# Regenerating the evidence: see LIB/gen/README.md ("Stub policy").
